paragraphs: We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing treatments for dermatological diseases with high unmet medical needs. Our current portfolio is comprised of highly differentiated topical and systemic treatments with significant potential to treat immune-mediated dermatological diseases and conditions. We believe we have built a leading platform for dermatologic product development and commercialization. Our strategy is to focus on validated biological targets, and to use our drug development platform and deep dermatology expertise to develop and commercialize differentiated products that have the potential to address the major shortcomings of existing therapies in our targeted indications. We believe this strategy uniquely positions us to rapidly advance our goal of bridging the treatment innovation gap in dermatology, while maximizing our probability of technical success and financial resources.

We launched our lead product, ZORYVE cream 0.3%, in August 2022 after obtaining our initial FDA approval for the treatment of plaque psoriasis, including psoriasis in the intertriginous areas (e.g. groin or axillae), in individuals 12 years of age or older. ZORYVE cream 0.3% is a once-daily topical formulation of roflumilast, a highly potent and selective phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor. ZORYVE cream 0.3% is approved for once-daily topical treatment of mild, moderate, and severe plaque psoriasis with no limitations on location or duration of use. In October 2023, we received FDA approval for an expanded indication in plaque psoriasis down to 6 years of age. In November 2025, our supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) was accepted for filing by the FDA to potentially expand the indication of ZORYVE cream 0.3% for the treatment of plaque psoriasis in children down to the age of 2, with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date set for June 29, 2026. In June 2023, we had our first commercial launch outside of the United States following Health Canada approval of ZORYVE cream 0.3% for the treatment of plaque psoriasis in individuals 12 years or age or older. In February 2026, Health Canada accepted our Supplement to a New Drug Submission (SNDS) for ZORYVE cream 0.3% for individuals down to 2 years old.

In December 2023, we received FDA approval for ZORYVE foam 0.3% for the treatment of seborrheic dermatitis in individuals aged 9 years and older, with no limitation on severity, location, or duration of use. ZORYVE foam is a once-daily steroid-free foam and, as a PDE4 inhibitor, was the first drug approved for the treatment of seborrheic dermatitis with a new mechanism of action in over two decades. ZORYVE foam became commercially available in the United States in January 2024 and became commercially available in Canada in December 2024 following approval by Health Canada. We received FDA approval for ZORYVE foam for the treatment of plaque psoriasis of the scalp and body in adults and adolescents ages 12 and older in May 2025, followed by commercial launch in the United States in June 2025. ZORYVE foam for the treatment of plaque psoriasis of the scalp and body in adults and adolescents ages 12 and older was also approved by Health Canada in October 2025, followed by commercial launch in November 2025.

We also received FDA approval for, and commercially launched, ZORYVE cream 0.15% in July 2024 for the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older, with no limitation on location, body surface area treated, concomitant use, or duration of use specified in the approved labelling. ZORYVE cream 0.15% was also approved by Health Canada in March 2025 and commercially launched in April 2025. We also received FDA approval for, and commercially launched, ZORYVE cream 0.05% for the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in children 2 to 5 years of age in October 2025. ZORYVE cream 0.15% and ZORYVE cream 0.05% are once-daily, steroid-free creams that provide rapid disease clearance and significant reduction in itch, and have been specifically developed to be treatment options for long-term disease control. In February 2026, we announced positive topline data for INTEGUMENT-INFANT, a Phase 2 study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of investigational ZORYVE cream 0.05% in infants as young as 3 months to less than 2 years with atopic dermatitis. We intend to submit an sNDA to the FDA in the second quarter of 2026 based on the results of this trial to potentially expand the indication for ZORYVE cream 0.05% for the treatment of infants with atopic dermatitis down to the age of 3 months.

In July 2024, we entered into a promotion agreement with Kowa Pharmaceuticals America, Inc. (Kowa) to leverage Kowa's primary care sales force to exclusively market and promote ZORYVE in the United States to primary care practitioners and pediatricians for all FDA-approved indications until at least July 2029. Under the terms of the agreement, Kowa will receive a commission from net sales attributed to Kowa. Promotion of ZORYVE in primary care and pediatrics under the Kowa agreement began in late September 2024. Effective January 23, 2026, we mutually agreed to terminate the promotion agreement. Following this termination, Kowa ceased all sales and promotions of ZORYVE and we will not be required to make any further payments to Kowa.

In August 2023, we entered into a strategic collaboration and licensing agreement (the Huadong Agreement) for topical roflumilast in Greater China and Southeast Asia with Hangzhou Zhongmei Huadong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Huadong). a wholly owned subsidiary of Huadong Medicine Co., Ltd. In February 2024, we entered into a a strategic collaboration and licensing agreement (the Sato Agreement) for topical roflumilast in Japan with Sato Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.(Sato).

In September 2022, we acquired Ducentis BioTherapeutics LTD (Ducentis) and its lead asset, DS-234 (now ARQ-234), a fusion protein that is a potent and highly selective checkpoint agonist of the CD200 Receptor (CD200R). We plan to develop ARQ-234 in atopic dermatitis, where we believe it could be a highly complementary biologic treatment option to ZORYVE cream 0.15% in that indication, if approved. ARQ-234 could potentially be used to treat other inflammatory conditions as well. We submitted an Investigational New Drug application (IND) to the FDA in July 2025, and anticipate commencing a Phase 1 study of ARQ-234 in the first quarter of 2026.

In July 2018, we executed a licensing agreement with AstraZeneca AB (AstraZeneca) for exclusive worldwide rights to roflumilast as a topical product in humans solely for dermatological indications. Moreover, we have our own intellectual property portfolio around topical uses of roflumilast, with issued and pending formulation, pharmacokinetic, and method-of-use patents in the United States and other jurisdictions from several distinct patent families, which provides us with exclusivity in the United States for our product cream formulation through 2037 and foam formulation through 2042.

Dermatological diseases such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and seborrheic dermatitis affect hundreds of millions of people worldwide each year, impacting their quality of life, and physical, functional, and emotional well-being. There are many approved treatments for these conditions, but a large opportunity remains due to issues with existing treatments. Topical treatments are used for nearly all patients, but existing topicals are limited by one or more of the following: modest response rates, side effects, patient adherence, application site restrictions, and limits on duration of therapy. Topical corticosteroids (TCS) are commonly used as the first-line therapy for the treatment of inflammatory skin conditions such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and seborrheic dermatitis. While many patients see improvements, extended use of TCS carries the risk of a variety of significant side effects. The localized side effects of extended use of TCS at the site of application, such as skin barrier damage and striae, have long been established. More recently, there is an increasing appreciation for the potential systemic side effects of prolonged TCS use, such as hyperglycemia, adrenal insufficiency, and osteoporosis. As a result, TCS are typically used intermittently for brief periods, making them an insufficient therapeutic option for inflammatory skin diseases that are chronic in nature. In psoriasis, vitamin D analogs are also used, but have lower response rates than TCS and are frequently irritating. Topical tapinarof (Vtama®) was approved in May 2022 for the treatment of adults with plaque psoriasis and in December 2024 for adults and children with atopic dermatitis, but this non-steroidal agent also carries significant application site reactions. In atopic dermatitis, topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCIs) and crisaborole (Eucrisa®), a topical non-steroidal PDE4 inhibitor, are used, but have lower response rates than TCS and are associated with application site burning. TCIs also have a boxed warning for cancer risk. Topical ruxolitinib (Opzelura®) was approved for the treatment of atopic dermatitis in September 2021, but carries an extensive boxed warning for numerous severe side effects, is limited to short-term, intermittent use, and is contraindicated for concomitant use with systemic therapies. In seborrheic dermatitis, in addition to TCS, topical antifungals are commonly used, but have limited efficacy.

Biologic and systemic therapies are also available for some diseases, but are typically indicated for a small percentage of the affected population with more severe disease. Importantly, most patients on biologic and systemic therapies for inflammatory skin conditions still require adjunctive topical therapies to treat residual disease and occasional flaring of symptoms. Biologics for psoriasis have shown impressive response rates but are only indicated for a minority of patients with moderate-to-severe forms and can often leave patients with some degree of residual disease. Treatment with oral systemic therapies such as methotrexate and apremilast (Otezla®) has also been limited due to modest symptomatic improvement and the frequency of adverse events. In atopic dermatitis, where biologic and systemic therapies have shown lower response rates, we see opportunity to both supplement
current therapies and to continue to advance the standard of care for patients, for example with regard to response rates and dosing frequency.

Given the limitations associated with existing treatments, we believe patients with inflammatory skin conditions and their dermatologists are dissatisfied with their current treatment options. We believe that there is a significant opportunity to leverage developments in other fields of medicine, particularly inflammation and immunology, to address the significant need for effective chronic treatments in immuno-dermatology. Our primary focus since our founding has been to address patients' significant need for innovative treatments that directly target molecular mediators of disease, have the potential to show significant symptomatic improvement, maintain a low risk of toxicity or side effects, and are suitable for chronic use on all areas of the body. Based on market research and our internal estimates, we estimate there is an overall actively prescription-treated patient market of approximately 17.0 million patients in the United States that are treated with topical therapies for plaque psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis, and atopic dermatitis, with approximately 8.4 million treated in dermatology offices and the remaining approximately 8.6 million treated outside dermatology. Of the patients that are treated in dermatology offices, we estimate that approximately 3.7 million of these patients are covered by Medicare or Medicaid, while approximately 4.7 million are covered by private payers. Patients that are treated outside of dermatology offices are primarily treated by primary care providers and pediatricians, and the ratio of commercial to government insurance is similar.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Condition, and Capital Requirements
Our operating results may fluctuate significantly, which makes our future operating results difficult to predict, and could cause our future operating results to fall below expectations.

Our estimated market opportunities are subject to numerous uncertainties and may prove to be inaccurate. If we have overestimated the size of our market opportunities, our future growth may be limited.
Changes in corporate governance policies and practices may impact our business.
Risks Related to Development and Commercialization
The sales, marketing, and distribution of ZORYVE or any future approved products may be unsuccessful or less successful than anticipated.
Our business is dependent on the successful commercialization of ZORYVE and the development, regulatory approval, and commercialization of our current product candidates.

Even if our product candidates receive marketing approval, they may fail to achieve market acceptance by physicians, patients, third-party payers, or others in the medical community necessary for commercial success.

Enrollment and retention of subjects in clinical trials is expensive and time-consuming and may result in additional costs and delays in our product development activities, or in the failure of such activities.
paragraphs: This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains forward-looking information based on our current expectations. Because our business is subject to many risks and our actual results may differ materially from any forward-looking statements made by or on behalf of us, this section includes a discussion of important factors that could affect our business, operating results, financial condition, and the trading price of our common stock. This discussion should be read in conjunction with the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations". The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, prospects, and stock price. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations.

We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company with four products approved for commercial sale. We have incurred significant losses since our inception and could incur losses in the future, which, together with our limited history as a commercial-stage company, makes it difficult to assess our future viability.

Biopharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. We have a limited history as a commercial-stage company upon which you can evaluate our business and prospects, and have not yet demonstrated an ability to successfully overcome many of the risks and uncertainties frequently encountered by companies in new and rapidly evolving fields. Our operations to date include organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, identifying potential product candidates, establishing licensing arrangements, undertaking various research and nonclinical studies, conducting clinical trials, establishing manufacturing and supply operations, and preparing for and launching commercialization activities. We have incurred losses in each year since our inception in June 2016. Our net loss for the year ended December 31, 2025 was approximately $16.1 million. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1,138.1 million. We commercially launched our first product, ZORYVE cream 0.3%, in August 2022; our second product, ZORYVE foam, in late January 2024; our third product, ZORYVE cream 0.15%, in July 2024; and our fourth product, ZORYVE cream 0.05%, in October 2025. We have generally and may incur losses until our revenue from product sales of ZORYVE and any other approved products exceeds expenses. We cannot anticipate when we will achieve sustained profitability. We will continue to incur research and development and other expenses related to our ongoing operations, our commercialization efforts, and the development of our product candidates. Losses have had and may have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital. In addition, we may
encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays, and other known or unknown factors in achieving our business objectives.

Due to the ongoing commercialization of products approved for commercial sale, and our development strategy and continued development of our pipeline of product candidates through clinical trials, our capital requirements are difficult to predict and may change. We may require substantial additional financing to achieve our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital if or when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce, or terminate certain operations or efforts.

We expect to continue to expend substantial resources in connection with our commercialization efforts, the development of our current product candidates, the maintenance and expansion of our business operations and capabilities, and the development or acquisition of additional product candidates. These expenditures will include costs associated with marketing and selling any products approved for sale, including ZORYVE, conducting non-clinical studies and clinical trials, obtaining regulatory approvals, securing manufacturing and supply of product candidates, costs associated with in-licensing dermatology assets consistent with our core strategy, and other unanticipated costs. Because the outcome of any nonclinical study or clinical trial is highly uncertain, we cannot reasonably estimate the actual amounts necessary to successfully complete the development and commercialization of any of our product candidates. Similarly, due to the complexities of our recent transition to a commercial-stage company, it is challenging to estimate the actual amounts necessary to successfully commercialize any products approved for sale. paragraphs: 本公司為一家商業階段的生技藥品公司，專注於開發與商業化治療具有重大未滿足醫療需求的皮膚科疾病之療法。本公司目前的產品組合包含高度差異化的局部與全身性治療藥物，具有顯著潛力用以治療免疫介導的皮膚科疾病與症狀。本公司認為已建立一個領先的皮膚科產品開發與商業化平台。本公司策略為聚焦於已驗證的生物標的，並運用本公司藥物開發平台與深厚的皮膚科專業知識，開發與商業化具差異化的產品，這些產品有潛力解決本公司目標適應症中現有療法的主要缺陷。本公司認為此策略獨特地使本公司能快速實現橋接皮膚科治療創新缺口的目標，同時最大化技術成功的機率與財務資源。

本公司於2022年8月推出領先產品ZORYVE乳霜0.3%，在取得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准用以治療斑塊型銀屑病，包括陰部或腋下等間隙性銀屑病（例如：12歲以上之個體）後。ZORYVE乳霜0.3%為一種每日一次的局部製劑，含有高度強效且選擇性磷酸二酯酶-4（PDE4）抑制劑roflumilast。ZORYVE乳霜0.3%核准用於每日一次的局部治療輕度、中度及重度斑塊型銀屑病，且無使用部位或使用時長的限制。2023年10月，本公司取得FDA核准擴大適應症至6歲以上之斑塊型銀屑病。2025年11月，本公司提交的補充新藥申請（sNDA）獲FDA接受審查，潛在擴大ZORYVE乳霜0.3%用於治療2歲以下兒童的斑塊型銀屑病，預計行動日期為2026年6月29日。2023年6月，本公司在美國以外地區首次商業發售，隨Health Canada核准ZORYVE乳霜0.3%用於治療12歲以上之斑塊型銀屑病。2026年2月，Health Canada接受本公司提交的補充新藥申請（SNDS）用於ZORYVE乳霜0.3%治療2歲以下兒童。

2023年12月，本公司取得FDA核准ZORYVE泡沫0.3%用於治療脂溢性皮膚炎，適用於9歲以上之個體，無嚴重程度、使用部位或使用時長的限制。ZORYVE泡沫為一種每日一次的不含類固醇泡沫，作為PDE4抑制劑，是近二十年來首款核准用以治療脂溢性皮膚炎且具有新機制的藥物。ZORYVE泡沫於2024年1月在美國上市，並於2024年12月經Health Canada核准後在加拿大上市。本公司於2025年5月取得FDA核准ZORYVE泡沫用於治療成人及12歲以上青少年的頭部與全身斑塊型銀屑病，隨後於2025年6月在美國上市。ZORYVE泡沫用於治療成人及12歲以上青少年的頭部與全身斑塊型銀屑病亦於2025年10月經Health Canada核准，隨後於2025年11月上市。

本公司亦於2024年7月取得FDA核准並商業發售ZORYVE乳霜0.15%，用於治療成人及6歲以上兒童的輕度至中度異位性皮膚炎，無使用部位、治療體表面積、同時使用藥物或使用時長的限制。ZORYVE乳霜0.15%亦於2025年3月經Health Canada核准，並於2025年4月商業發售。本公司亦於2025年10月取得FDA核准並商業發售ZORYVE乳霜0.05%，用於治療2至5歲兒童的輕度至中度異位性皮膚炎。ZORYVE乳霜0.15%與ZORYVE乳霜0.05%為每日一次、不含類固醇乳霜，可快速改善病情並顯著減輕癢感，並專門開發為長期控制疾病之治療選項。2026年2月，本公司宣佈INTEGUMENT-INFANT試驗的初步數據為正面，此為評估正在研究中的ZORYVE乳霜0.05%在3個月至未滿2歲的異位性皮膚炎嬰兒中的安全性與有效性之第二期試驗。本公司預計於2026年第二季向FDA提交sNDA，以根據此試驗結果潛在擴大ZORYVE乳霜0.05%用於治療異位性皮膚炎的適應症至3個月以下的嬰兒。

2024年7月，本公司與Kowa Pharmaceuticals America, Inc.（Kowa）簽訂促銷協議，以利用Kowa的門診醫療銷售團隊專門在美國為所有FDA核准適應症向門診醫師與小兒科醫師推廣與銷售ZORYVE，直至至少2029年7月。根據協議條款，Kowa將從淨銷售額中取得佣金。2024年9月下旬，ZORYVE在門診與小兒科的促銷活動開始。自2026年1月23日起，本公司與Kowa mutually agreed to terminate the promotion agreement。此後，Kowa停止所有ZORYVE的銷售與促銷，本公司亦無需再向Kowa支付任何費用。

2023年8月，本公司與Hangzhou Zhongmei Huadong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.（Huadong）簽訂戰略合作與授權協議（Huadong Agreement），授權 topical roflumilast 在中國大陸與東南亞地區。Huadong為Huadong Medicine Co., Ltd.的全資子公司。2024年2月，本公司與Sato Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.（Sato）簽訂戰略合作與授權協議（Sato Agreement），授權 topical roflumilast 在日本地區。

2022年9月，本公司取得Ducentis BioTherapeutics LTD（Ducentis）及其領先資產DS-234（現為ARQ-234）的授權，ARQ-234為一種強效且高度選擇性的CD200受體（CD200R）檢查點活化蛋白。本公司計畫在異位性皮膚炎中開發ARQ-234，認為其可能成為ZORYVE乳霜0.15%在該適應症中的高度補充生物治療選項，若獲得核准。ARQ-234可能還可用於治療其他發炎性疾病。本公司於2025年7月向FDA提交新藥研究申請（IND），預計於2026年第一季開始ARQ-234的第一期試驗。

2018年7月，本公司與AstraZeneca AB（AstraZeneca）簽訂授權協議，取得roflumilast作為局部產品在人類中專門用於皮膚科適應症的全球獨家權。此外，本公司擁有關於roflumilast局部使用之智慧財產權組合，包含已發明及待審的製劑、藥代動力學及使用方法專利，於美國及其他司法管轄區，來自幾個不同的專利家族，使本公司在美國的產品乳霜製劑專利獨佔權至2037年，泡沫製劑專利獨佔權至2042年。

皮膚科疾病如銀屑病、異位性皮膚炎與脂漏性皮膚炎，每年影響全球數百萬人，影響其生活品質與身體、功能與情緒健康。這些疾病有許多核准的治療方式，但因現有治療方式的問題，仍有相當大的發展空間。近似所有病患都會使用局部治療，但現有局部治療方式受限於以下一個或多個因素：治療反應率有限、副作用、病患依從性、使用部位限制，以及治療持續時間的限制。局部類固醇（Topical Corticosteroids, TCS）常被用作治療發炎性皮膚疾病如銀屑病、異位性皮膚炎與脂漏性皮膚炎的第一線療法。雖然許多病患會見到改善，但長期使用TCS會導致多種重大副作用的風險。長期使用TCS在使用部位的局部副作用，如皮膚屏障損傷與條紋，早已被廣泛認知。較近來，人們對長期使用TCS可能導致的系統性副作用，如高血糖、腎上腺功能不足與骨質疏鬆，也開始有更深入的認識。因此，TCS通常會間歇性地短時間使用，使其成為治療慢性發炎性皮膚疾病的不充分療法。在銀屑病中，維生素D類似物也常被使用，但其治療反應率低於TCS，且常會引起刺激。局部Tapinarof（Vtama®）於2022年5月核准用於治療成人斑塊型銀屑病，於2024年12月核准用於治療成人與兒童異位性皮膚炎，但此非類固醇藥物也會導致顯著的使用部位反應。在異位性皮膚炎中，局部環孢素抑制劑（Topical Calcineurin Inhibitors, TCIs）與Crisaborole（Eucrisa®），一種局部非類固醇PDE4抑制劑，也常被使用，但其治療反應率低於TCS，且與使用部位灼熱感有關。TCIs也有一個黑框警告，指出與癌症風險相關。局部Ruxolitinib（Opzelura®）於2021年9月核准用於治療異位性皮膚炎，但其有廣泛的黑框警告，指出多種嚴重副作用，僅限短時間間歇性使用，且不建議與系統性治療同時使用。在脂漏性皮膚炎中，除了TCS，局部抗真菌藥物也常被使用，但其療效有限。

生物製劑與系統性治療方式也適用於某些疾病，但通常僅適用於受影響人口中一小部分具有較嚴重疾病的病患。重要的是，大多數接受生物製劑與系統性治療的發炎性皮膚疾病病患，仍需輔以局部治療來治療殘餘疾病與偶發症狀發作。銀屑病的生物製劑已顯示出驚人的治療反應率，但僅適用於少數具有中度至重度形式的病患，且常會留下一定程度的殘餘疾病。口服系統性治療如甲氨蝶呤與阿普斯特（Otezla®）的治療也因治療反應率有限與副作用頻繁而受到限制。在異位性皮膚炎中，生物製劑與系統性治療的治療反應率較低，我們看到機會不僅是補充現有治療方式，也持續提升患者的治療標準，例如在治療反應率與給藥頻率方面。
目前治療方式與持續提升患者的治療標準，例如在治療反應率與給藥頻率方面。

考量現有治療方式的限制，我們認為患有發炎性皮膚疾病的患者及其皮膚科醫師對目前的治療選項感到不滿意。我們認為，可以透過其他醫學領域的發展，特別是發炎與免疫學，來解決免疫皮膚學領域對有效慢性治療的重大需求。自公司成立以來，我們的主要重點一直在解決患者對創新治療方式的重大需求，這些治療方式能直接針對疾病的分子媒介，有潛力顯示顯著的症狀改善，維持低毒性或副作用的風險，且適合全身各部位的長期使用。根據市場研究及我們的內部估計，我們估計美國有約 17.0 百萬名患者接受局部治療，用以治療斑塊狀銀屑病、脂溢性皮膚炎及過敏性皮膚炎，其中約 8.4 百萬名患者是在皮膚科診所接受治療，剩餘約 8.6 百萬名患者是在皮膚科診所以外的場所接受治療。在皮膚科診所接受治療的患者中，我們估計約 3.7 百萬名患者是由 medicare 或 medicaid 覆蓋，而約 4.7 百萬名患者是由私人付款者覆蓋。在皮膚科診所以外接受治療的患者，主要是由一般門診醫師及小兒科醫師治療，且商業保險與政府保險的比例相似。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們經審計之財務報表及相關附註一同閱讀，這些財務報表及附註出現在本年度報告表 10-K 其他處。有關 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年比較之討論，請參閱本年度報告表 10-K 中第二部分，第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」。部分包含於本討論與分析中或出現在本年度報告表 10-K 其他處之資訊，包括有關我們業務之計畫、目標、預期、預測與策略之資訊，包含風險與不確定性之向前看聲明。由於許多因素，包括下列所識別之因素及本年度報告表 10-K 中「風險因素」部分所載之因素，我們實際結果及選定事件之時間可能與本討論與分析中所包含之向前看聲明有重大差異。請同時參閱「向前看聲明特別說明」部分。

我們是一家商業階段之生技藥品公司，專注於開發與商業化治療具有高未滿足醫療需求之皮膚疾病之藥物。我們目前之產品組合包含高度差異化之局部與系統性治療，具有治療免疫介導之皮膚疾病與症狀之顯著潛力。我們相信我們已建立一個領導之平台，用以開發與商業化皮膚科產品。我們的策略為專注於已驗證之生物標的，並運用我們之藥物開發平台與深厚的皮膚科專業知識，開發與商業化差異化產品，這些產品有潛力解決我們目標適應症中現有治療之主要缺點。我們相信此策略獨特地使我們能快速進展我們彌合皮膚科治療創新缺口之目標，同時最大化我們之技術成功機率與財務資源。

我們於 2022 年 8 月推出我們之主要產品 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3%，在取得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准用以治療斑塊型銀屑病，包括銀屑病在摩擦部位（例如腹股溝或腋下）之 12 歲或以上年齡層個體後。ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3% 是一種每日一次之局部製劑，含有高度強效且選擇性之磷酸二酯酶-4（PDE4）抑制劑 roflumilast。ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3% 已核准用以每日一次之局部治療輕度、中度及重度斑塊型銀屑病，無使用部位或使用時長之限制。2023 年 10 月，我們取得 FDA 核准，將適用範圍擴展至 6 歲或以上年齡層之斑塊型銀屑病。2025 年 11 月，我們的補充新藥申請（sNDA）被 FDA 接受為可提交，以潛在擴展 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3% 用以治療 2 歲以下年齡層之斑塊型銀屑病，其處方藥使用者費用法案（PDUFA）目標行動日期為 2026 年 6 月 29 日。2023 年 6 月，我們在美國以外的地區進行首次商業發售，隨 Health Canada 核准 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3% 用以治療 12 歲或以上年齡層之斑塊型銀屑病。2026 年 2 月，Health Canada 接受我們針對 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.3% 的補充新藥提交（SNDS）用以治療 2 歲以下年齡層之個體。

2023 年 12 月，我們取得 FDA 核准 ZORYVE 泡沫 0.3% 用以治療 9 歲或以上年齡層之脂溢性皮膚炎，無嚴重程度、使用部位或使用時長之限制。ZORYVE 泡沫是一種每日一次之不含類固醇泡沫，作為 PDE4 抑制劑，是近二十年來首款核准用以治療脂溢性皮膚炎且具有新機製作用之藥物。ZORYVE 泡沫於 2024 年 1 月在美國上市，並於 2024 年 12 月經 Health Canada 核准後在加拿大上市。我們於 2025 年 5 月取得 FDA 核准 ZORYVE 泡沫用以治療成人及 12 歲以上青少年之頭部及身體斑塊型銀屑病，隨後於 2025 年 6 月在美國進行商業發售。ZORYVE 泡沫用以治療成人及 12 歲以上青少年之頭部及身體斑塊型銀屑病亦於 2025 年 10 月經 Health Canada 核准，隨後於 2025 年 11 月進行商業發售。

我們亦於 2024 年 7 月取得 FDA 核准，並進行商業發售，ZORYVE 創面霜 0.15% 用以治療成人及 6 歲以上兒童之輕度至中度異位性皮膚炎，無使用部位、治療體表面積、同時使用藥物或使用時長之限制。ZORYVE 創面霜 0.15% 亦於 2025 年 3 月經 Health Canada 核准，並於 2025 年 4 月進行商業發售。我們亦於 2025 年 10 月取得 FDA 核准，並進行商業發售，ZORYVE 創面霜 0.05% 用以治療 2 至 5 歲兒童之輕度至中度異位性皮膚炎。ZORYVE 創面霜 0.15% 與 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.05% 是每日一次、不含類固醇之乳霜，可快速改善病情並顯著減少癢感，並專門開發為長期疾病控制之治療選項。2026 年 2 月，我們宣佈 INTEGUMENT-INFANT 研究的初步數據，該研究評估 Investigational ZORYVE 創面霜 0.05% 在 3 個月至 2 歲以下異位性皮膚炎嬰兒之安全性與有效性。
我們計畫於 2026 年第二季向 FDA 提交 sNDA，基於此試驗結果，以潛在擴展 ZORYVE 創面霜 0.05% 用以治療異位性皮膚炎嬰兒之適用範圍至 3 個月以下年齡。

2024 年 7 月，我們與 Kowa Pharmaceuticals America, Inc.（Kowa）簽訂促銷協議，利用 Kowa 之主要門診銷售團隊專門在美國為所有 FDA 核准適應症向主要門診醫師及小兒科醫師促銷 ZORYVE，直至至少 2029 年 7 月。根據協議條款，Kowa 將從歸屬 Kowa 之淨銷售額中取得佣金。根據協議，Kowa 於 2024 年 9 月下旬開始促銷 ZORYVE 用於主要門診及小兒科。自 2026 年 1 月 23 日起，我們雙方同意終止促銷協議。此後，Kowa 停止所有 ZORYVE 之銷售與促銷，我們亦無需再向 Kowa 支付任何進一步費用。

2023 年 8 月，我們與 Hangzhou Zhongmei Huadong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.（Huadong）簽訂戰略合作與授權協議（Huadong 協議），授權 topical roflumilast 在中國大陸與東南亞地區。Huadong 是 Huadong Medicine Co., Ltd. 之全資子公司。2024 年 2 月，我們與 Sato Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.（Sato）簽訂戰略合作與授權協議（Sato 協議），授權 topical roflumilast 在日本地區。

2022年9月，本公司取得Ducentis BioTherapeutics LTD（Ducentis）及其主要資產DS-234（現為ARQ-234），一種融合蛋白，為CD200受體（CD200R）的強效且高度選擇性檢查點活化劑。本公司計畫在異位性皮膚炎領域開發ARQ-234，若ZORYVE乳膏0.15%在該適應症獲准上市，本公司認為ARQ-234可能成為高度補充性的生物製劑治療選項。ARQ-234也可能用於治療其他發炎性疾病。本公司於2025年7月向FDA提交了新藥臨牀試驗申請（IND），預計於2026年第一季開始進行ARQ-234的第1期試驗。

2018年7月，本公司與AstraZeneca AB（AstraZeneca）簽訂授權協議，取得roflumilast作為人用局部產品的獨家全球權利，僅限於皮膚科適應症。此外，本公司擁有關於roflumilast局部使用之智慧財產權組合，包含已發行及待審的製劑、藥代動力學及使用方法專利，於美國及其他司法管轄區來自多個不同專利家族，使本公司在美國的產品乳膏製劑享有至2037年的獨佔權，泡沫製劑則享有至2042年的獨佔權。

本公司自設立以來每年均產生年度淨虧損，包括截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日止之淨虧損分別為16.1百萬美元、140.0百萬美元及262.1百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為1,138.1百萬美元，並持有現金、現金等價物、限制性現金及市場性證券共221.3百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司根據貸款協議尚有100.0百萬美元貸款餘額。本公司於2024年10月使用現有現金償還貸款協議本金100.0百萬美元，並保留於界定期間內重新提款之權利。

未來各期間的淨收入或淨虧損程度尚無法預測，本公司可能持續產生淨虧損。本公司預期在商業化ZORYVE、並推進產品候選藥物及標籤擴展通過臨牀試驗、審批及商業化過程時，持續產生重大支出。本公司預期產生與ZORYVE銷售、行銷、製造及分銷相關的商業化支出，同時將臨牀開發支出集中於ARQ-234及ZORYVE標籤擴展。雖然本公司不預期需要透過融資或其他來源支應目前計畫的運作，但若本公司現有現金及市場性證券餘額及預期未來營運現金流不足以支應這些支出，本公司可能需要透過股票或債務融資或其他來源，例如未來潛在的合作協議，支應運作。本公司可能無法在可接受的條件或任何情況下取得足夠資金。若無法在需要時取得足夠資金，將對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
2022年8月，配合本公司首款FDA核准產品的上市，本公司開始認列產品銷售收入，扣除相關扣除項後的淨收入。以下為本公司開始認列產品銷售收入，扣除相關扣除項後的時間段，與各產品及適應症的上市相關：

paragraphs: 本年度10-K表報表包含基於我們目前預期的展望性資訊。因為我們的業務面臨許多風險，且實際結果可能與任何展望性陳述有重大差異，本節包含可能影響我們業務、營運成果、財務狀況及普通股交易價格的重要因素討論。此討論應與本年度10-K表報表的其他資訊一併閱讀，包括財務報表及相關附註與「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」。上述任何事件或發展的發生，可能對我們的業務、營運成果、財務狀況、前景及股票價格造成重大不利影響。此外，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能影響我們的業務運作。
我們是一家商業階段的生物科技公司，擁有四種已核准上市銷售的產品。自我們成立以來，我們已產生顯著虧損，未來也可能產生虧損，加上我們作為商業階段公司的有限歷史，使我們難以評估未來的生存能力。

生技藥品開發是一項高度投機的業務，並涉及相當程度的風險。本公司在商業階段的經營歷史有限，因此您無法根據本公司業務與前景進行評估，且尚未證明本公司能成功克服許多新興且快速發展領域中常見的風險與不確定性。本公司至今的業務活動包括籌組與組建本公司、業務規劃、籌資、尋找潛在產品候選物、建立授權協議、進行各種研究與非臨牀研究、進行臨牀試驗、建立製造與供應作業，以及準備與啟動商業化活動。本公司自2016年6月成立以來，每個年度均產生虧損。本公司2025年12月31日財務年度的淨虧損約為16.1 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為1,138.1 百萬美元。本公司於2022年8月商業化推出首款產品ZORYVE乳霜0.3%；於2024年1月底推出第二款產品ZORYVE泡沫劑；於2024年7月推出第三款產品ZORYVE乳霜0.15%；於2025年10月推出第四款產品ZORYVE乳霜0.05%。本公司通常且可能持續產生虧損，直到本公司來自ZORYVE產品及任何其他核准產品的銷售收入超過費用。本公司無法預測何時能實現持續獲利。本公司將持續產生與持續營運、商業化努力及產品候選物開發相關的研究與開發及其他費用。虧損已對股東權益與營運資金產生並可能繼續產生負面影響。此外，本公司可能
遭遇未預見的費用、困難、複雜情況、延誤及其他已知或未知因素，以實現我們的業務目標。
由於持續商業化已核准上市銷售的產品，以及我們的發展策略與持續開發產品候選物的臨牀試驗，我們的資金需求難以預測且可能變化。我們可能需要大量額外資金以實現目標，若無法在需要時以可接受的條件或完全無法取得必要資金，可能會迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止某些運作或努力。

我們預期會持續投入大量資源，用於商業化努力、目前產品候選物的開發、維護與擴展我們的業務運作與能力，以及開發或取得其他產品候選物。這些支出將包括行銷與銷售任何核准上市產品（包括ZORYVE）的費用、進行非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗、取得監管核准、確保產品候選物的製造與供應、與我們核心策略一致的皮膚科資產進授權費用，以及其他未預見的費用。由於任何非臨牀研究或臨牀試驗的結果極為不確定，我們無法合理預估成功完成任何產品候選物開發與商業化所需的實際金額。同樣地，由於我們最近轉型為商業階段公司的複雜性，難以預估成功商業化任何核准上市產品所需的實際金額。我們的營運費用與資金需求難以預測，取決於許多因素，並受以下因素影響，且受到相關假設的影響：
